topic: Competitive teardown — BNB agent marketplaces and agent trust/evidence layers (Build the Era hackathon + broader category), observed 18 Aug 2026
executive_summary:
All six named repos exist and are public — none 404'd. But the six you named are not the competitive frontier. GitHub search surfaced three entrants that are materially ahead: **winsznx/mandate** (369 files, contract DEPLOYED and Sourcify-verified on BSC testnet, trial→authority-ceiling→mandate enforcement), **kaizenbnb/bnb-agent-marketplace** (real BSC-testnet work transactions, independently verified onchain), and **gilbertsahumada** (hexagonal TS, 100+ files, trust8004 integration).

The hard news for AiKi: **your four differentiators are already shipped and live, by third parties, for free.** trust8004.xyz's `/api/v2/agents/{id}/score` returns per-dimension scores each with an explicit `confidence` float (availability 0.55, activity 0.3, wallet 0.6, popularity 0.2) — that *is* confidence-weighted scoring, queryable today with no key. 8004scan's `scores/v5` v5.2 `v5_leaderboard_policy` ships five weighted dimensions with human-readable `explanation` strings, `health_status` liveness, and integrity tiers. winsznx/mandate ships mandate enforcement tiers on-chain: a `testedAuthorityHash` that is a *ceiling* on every derived authority, with `ReceiptDidNotPass` reverting on-chain so a failed trial can never back a live mandate. TermiX AACP already has staked evaluators with `PROGRAM`/`RUBRIC`/`HYBRID`/`CEX_CAPITAL` (TEE + Groth16 zkVM) strategy types.

What nobody has solved: the ValidationRegistry is empty (`total_validations: 0`, `total_validators: 0` globally, 743K agents), 100% of BSC feedback lacks any interaction proof, sybil-flagged feedback on BSC runs 96.3%, and the median cost to move an agent across a τ=90 trust threshold is **$0.0042**. Reputation on BSC is not weak — it is worthless. That is the real opening.

findings.claim: All six named repos exist and are public; two are effectively empty. airway/bnb-era-marketplace is a single 351-byte README with 1 commit — a name-squat, not a project.
findings.detail: gh API metadata, 18 Aug 2026. Ai-Rook/bnb-agent-marketplace: JS, 19 commits, 24 files, pushed 2026-08-16. 0xConsole/bnb-agent-marketplace: Python/FastAPI, 2 commits, 17 files, pushed 2026-08-15. airway/bnb-era-marketplace: 1 commit, 1 file (README.md, 351 bytes), no code, no language detected. daluoboda/agentlens: HTML/Python, 2 commits, 32 files, pushed 2026-08-11 (untouched for a week). alogotron/assay-bsc: 1 commit, 23 files, 20 of which are raw 8004scan probe JSON — README states plainly "marketplace interface not yet implemented". Lutviansyah/AgentEra: TypeScript/Next.js, 13 commits, 35 files, pushed 2026-08-17. None have a single star or fork. Total real engineering across all six is roughly one strong solo week.

findings.claim: DEPLOYED: winsznx/mandate has a MandateReceiptRegistry live on BSC testnet at 0x4c2b4d81a0b5ffb9b13f8c6b22fbbdc9d69da299 — I independently confirmed 7862 bytes of runtime code, exactly matching its declared deployedBytecodeSize, and the deploy tx receipt.
findings.detail: contracts/deployments/97.json declares address, txHash 0x3b3ff1dd0ca81fea3d40f6d13a65c5c4314f4243d80b643396c14874936cb05e, block 125782940, solc 0.8.28, sourcify VERIFIED. eth_getCode against bsc-testnet-rpc.publicnode.com returns 7862 bytes; eth_getTransactionReceipt on that hash returns status 0x1, contractAddress 0x4c2b4d81a0b5ffb9b13f8c6b22fbbdc9d69da299, block 125782940. Every declared field checks out. Deployed 2026-08-18T10:25Z — the same day the repo was created, 23 commits, 369 files. This is the only hackathon entrant with a purpose-built trust contract actually on chain.

findings.claim: winsznx/mandate has already built AiKi's "mandate enforcement tiers" — and put the enforcement on-chain rather than in application code.
findings.detail: contracts/src/IMandateReceiptRegistry.sol: struct Receipt carries testedAuthorityHash documented as "Ceiling on every authority derived from this receipt", plus trialSpecHash, scenarioHash, evaluatorHash, referenceModelHash, evidenceHash, agentVersionHash, snapshotBlock, and freshUntil ("After this the receipt is history, not current certification" — expiring liveness). struct Activation binds trialReceiptId → wallet → sessionKeyHash → grantedAuthorityHash + disclosureURI, so a verifier working from chain alone can fetch the granted AuthorityIR and evaluate the subset relation against the tested ceiling. error ReceiptDidNotPass(bytes32) is documented: "A failed trial can never back a live mandate. Enforced on-chain so the claim does not rest on application code." This is the mandate-tier design AiKi intended to differentiate on, shipped and verified.

findings.claim: winsznx/mandate also built the benchmark-derived performance layer: deterministic anvil fork-replay trials against an independent reference model, with machine-checkable pass/fail checks and full environment disclosure.
findings.detail: artifacts/evidence/20260818T125522Z/evidence-bundle.json records agentId 1842, category HEALTH_FACTOR, environment {anvilVersion "anvil Version: 1.7.1", chainId 97, forkBlock 125802737, forkBlockHash 0x885d3b77…, rpcSourceClass "archive", modifiedState true} and enumerates every state modification (anvil_setBalance FUND_GAS, anvil_impersonateAccount IMPERSONATE) with the explicit disclosure "no signature was produced and none is claimed". evaluator.checks are individually named and observable: reference-model-conclusive (observed AT_RISK), observation-is-current (observed block 125802743 — a liveness check that the agent reasoned about the block the trial presented), decision-matches-reference (PROPOSE), action-target-authorised, action-selector-authorised. Supporting code: services/trial-runner (evaluator.ts, observation.ts, independence.test.ts), services/authority-proof (phase7/expect-rejection.ts, spend-bucket.ts, attribution.ts, blockers.ts), apps/verifier (replay-adapters/health-factor.ts, steps-rejected.ts, cross-format.test.ts).

findings.claim: DEPLOYED: trust8004.xyz already serves confidence-weighted, per-dimension trust scores over a free unauthenticated API. AiKi's "confidence-weighted scoring" is not a differentiator — it is a live third-party endpoint.
findings.detail: GET https://trust8004.xyz/api/v2/agents/1/score?chainId=56 returned, today: total 48.8, tier "bronze", and dimensions each carrying score, weight, weighted AND an explicit confidence float — quality {57, w20, conf 1}, completeness {61, w15, conf 1}, availability {68, w20, conf 0.55}, freshness {34, w15, conf 1}, activity {0, w15, conf 0.3}, wallet {79, w10, conf 0.6}, popularity {32, w5, conf 0.2}. Also returns calculatedAt/expiresAt (5-minute TTL — score staleness is modelled), badges ["established"], activeReputationSystems [], and a null chaosChain slot. Sibling routes: /api/v2/agents?chainId=&limit=, /api/v2/agents/profile?chainId=&agentId=. The list response carries endpointHealth, mcpEndpoint, a2aEndpoint, x402support, storageMet…, specVersion, isLegacy. Endpoint paths recovered from gilbertsahumada/bnb-agent-marketplace src/trust8004/provider.ts lines 134/141/149, then called directly.

findings.claim: DEPLOYED: 8004scan ships a versioned, explainable 5-dimension scoring algorithm (v5.2, "v5_leaderboard_policy") plus liveness health-checks and endpoint verification — free, no key, and it already covers BSC.
findings.detail: GET https://api.8004scan.io/api/v1/agents/scores/v5/56/1 returns total_score 21.31, version "5.2", algorithm "v5_leaderboard_policy", with weighted dimensions: engagement (w 0.30), service (w 0.25), publisher (w 0.20), compliance (w 0.15), momentum (w 0.10), plus top-level multipliers / raw_scores / weights. Each dimension carries a natural-language explanation ("No A2A or MCP services. Add endpoints to unlock full scoring potential (capped at 30)") and structured details — service.details includes has_a2a, has_mcp, a2a_quality, mcp_quality, health_status "healthy", integrity_tier "no-core-service", discoverability_tier "metadata-only"; compliance.details includes is_endpoint_verified, parse_status, metadata_completeness_score, verification_bonus; publisher.details includes wallet_score, wallet_source, validation_score, certification_tier. The OpenAPI (148 paths) exposes POST /agents/{chain_id}/{token_id}/health-check (auth required), POST /agents/verify-endpoint/{chain_id}/{token_id}, GET /agents/{chain_id}/{token_id}/quality, GET /agents/score-history/{chain_id}/{token_id}, GET /status/freshness, and webhooks.

findings.claim: THE OPEN GAP: the ERC-8004 ValidationRegistry is globally unused. 8004scan reports total_validations 0 and total_validators 0 against 743,130 agents and 3,550,780 feedbacks.
findings.detail: GET https://api.8004scan.io/api/v1/stats/global (18 Aug 2026): total_agents 735138, total_users 401294, total_validators 0, total_feedbacks 3550780, total_validations 0, daily_new_agents 2220, daily_feedbacks 6648, average_feedback_score 80.99, average_validation_score null. Corroborated by the arXiv empirical study, which states "the Validation Registry had no confirmed mainnet deployment during our observation period" (through 13 May 2026). Separately, /status/freshness shows the agent_health component tracking only 46,847 records against 735,138 agents — under 7% of the registry has any health data at all, and the top-level freshness status was "down" when queried. Every subjective-feedback path is saturated; the objective-validation path is a greenfield with zero incumbents.

findings.claim: BSC reputation is not merely noisy, it is economically worthless: 96.3% of scored feedback on BSC is sybil-flagged, 100% lacks any interaction evidence, and the median cost to move an agent across a τ=90 trust threshold is $0.0042.
findings.detail: arXiv 2606.26028, measured through 13 May 2026 across Ethereum/BSC/Base. BSC: 90,145 agents registered, 83.4% (75,101) with valid registration files, but only ~4% classified "valid ERC-8004 with service" — i.e. a live service endpoint. 29,444 feedback records over 4,310 rated agents from just 76 unique reviewers. 59.2% of BSC reviewers sybil-flagged by shared funding provenance; 96.3% of non-revoked scored feedback sybil-flagged; 81.4% of rated agents affected; 77.9% of rated agents have NO valid feedback left after sybil removal. 100.0% of BSC feedback lacks payment proof or task linkage (Base: 99.3%, and only 6.2% of Base reviewers have any x402 payment history). Median manipulation cost per feedback record: BSC $0.0042, Base $0.0027, Ethereum $0.055 — and the median number of ceiling-valued ratings needed to cross τ=90 is 1. Caveat: this is peer research, not a primary spec; numbers are as of May 2026 and BSC has ~2.8× more agents now.

findings.claim: Ground truth on BSC registry scale, independently measured today: 257,906 ERC-8004 agents on chain 56 out of 743,130 platform-wide — so the widely quoted "200k/266k/737k BSC agents" in entrant READMEs are each wrong in different directions.
findings.detail: GET https://api.8004scan.io/api/v1/agents?chain_id=56&limit=1 → total 257906, items all chain_id 56. GET without chain_id → total 743130. Competing claims: Ai-Rook README "266,000+", AgentEra "200k", 0xConsole "737,000+ real BSC agents" (that is the ALL-CHAIN figure, not BSC), alogotron measured 247,808 on 2026-08-08, kaizenbnb "roughly 263,000". alogotron's 247,808→247,939 in five hours implies ~3,128 new BSC agents/day; the 8004scan global figure is 2,220/day platform-wide, so the two disagree and neither should be quoted without re-measuring. The BSC mainnet Identity Registry 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432 returns 130 bytes of code (a minimal/ERC-1967 proxy); the testnet registry 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e is likewise 130 bytes. Both verified live via eth_getCode.

findings.claim: LANDMINE, verified: the 8004scan list endpoint's chain filter is `chain_id`. Passing `chain=56` or `chain_ids=56` is silently ignored and returns Ethereum agents. 0xConsole's marketplace has this exact bug in production.
findings.detail: Measured today: ?chain_id=56&limit=1 → total 257906, chains {56}. ?chain=bsc&limit=1 → total 743130, chains {1}. ?chain_ids=56&limit=1 → total 743130, chains {1}. No error, no warning — just the wrong chain. 0xConsole/bnb-agent-marketplace README and app/scan_client.py both document and call `GET /api/v1/agents?chain=56`, so its "real BSC agent data" is actually unfiltered Ethereum-dominated data. RNWY exhibits the same class of failure: https://rnwy.com/api/agents?chain_id=56&limit=1 returned an agent with chain_id 100 (Gnosis). Any AiKi ingestion must assert the returned chain_id per row rather than trusting the query parameter.

findings.claim: Ai-Rook is the most complete of the six named repos and the only one with a real b402 merchant integration and a working BSC anchoring path — but its 'verified usage' moat is self-listing of its own services over localhost, not a general evidence layer.
findings.detail: Stack: Node/Express + node:sqlite + ethers, 24 files. Genuinely integrated, with paths: b402.js implements Binance's authenticated facilitator — RSA-SHA256 "Tesla" request signing over body+timestamp with X-Tesla-ClientId / SignAccessToken / Timestamp / Signature headers, POST /papi/v2/b402/verify then /papi/v2/b402/settle, envelope.code '000000' success check, fail-closed on settle. Uses @x402/core/http decodePaymentSignatureHeader. anchor.js anchors sha256(receipt) to BSC mainnet chainId 56 as a zero-value self-transfer with the hash in calldata, over a 6-RPC fallback list. altana-session.js uses @altananetwork/sdk v0.7.1 grantSession with call allowlist + spend caps + expiry + Keystore registration. reputation.js pulls 8004scan /api/v1/agents/{chain}/{id}. config.js carries the EIP-7201 slot 0xa040f782729de4970518741823ec1276cbcd41a0c7493f62d173341566a04e00 for IdentityRegistryStorage._lastId — a genuinely clever enumeration trick. The weakness: self-list.js sources "verified usage" from http://127.0.0.1:3051/api/trust, :3007, :3020, :3025 — its own boxes — and inserts them at negative agent_id (-59646) with is_self=1. Unfalsifiable by anyone else, and the anchored agent (59646) lives on eip155:8453 (Base), not BSC.

findings.claim: Lutviansyah/AgentEra is scaffolded end-to-end and its headline TermiX evidence is fabricated — but its Altana session grant/revoke on BSC testnet appears to be real.
findings.detail: lib/8004scan.ts is a hardcoded 6-element MOCK array with a literal comment "TODO: replace with real 8004scan Pro API when key available"; the successRate/ttft numbers rendered in the UI are invented constants. lib/x402.ts createX402Payment() returns {invoiceId: 'x402-'+agentId+'-'+Date.now(), status:'pending'} with "This scaffold just returns a mock invoice". The TermiX Agent Advantage Report claims 40.6× / 163× / 604× speedups; docs/termix-evidence/task1-with.json cites pool address "0x1b96b925b76a75d84c04d409fa170a2e382e8ad" — 39 hex chars, not a valid 20-byte address, which is the signature of LLM-generated evidence. The README does, however, link a specific Altana grant tx 0x59ff5f93… and revoke tx 0x7f0caa06… on BSC testnet 97 with a 10 USDT/day spend cap; I did not verify those two hashes. Treat AgentEra as a design mock with one real onchain thread.

findings.claim: kaizenbnb/bnb-agent-marketplace sets the honesty bar: real BSC-testnet work transactions that I independently confirmed onchain, instrumented end-to-end latency, and a written refusal to show the registry because it is spam.
findings.detail: 38 commits, 116 files, live at bnb-agent-marketplace.vercel.app. agents/AGENT_ADVANTAGE_REPORT.md states its methodology as a rule: "Every task is anchored on a real, verifiable BSC Testnet transaction, no hypothetical comparisons", labels every estimate as ESTIMATE, and measures the agent side with a MutationObserver on the live page: 402 returned 3 ms, Permit2 signed 28 ms, settlement+work 29,192 ms, total 29,416 ms; second run 26,307 ms. It then decomposes that honestly — ~0.9 s (3%) irreducible chain confirmation at 0.450 s block time, ~28.5 s (97%) Altana SDK relay orchestration — and explicitly declines to split the 28.5 s further "so it is reported as one measured block, not split by guesswork". I verified work tx 0xfa7d848f…9748: found, status 0x1, block 124619400, to 0xcb5cef3c54aa90e9a7ad602a258d3d360cc862b9 — exactly as claimed. README admits all 4 agents share one wallet, that the listings are curated not live, and that indexing the BSC registry found "no DeFi-native agents… Quack AI gasless bots, EvoEvo clones and meme-token spam". It also documents a fixed real bug: an earlier build let the client supply the x402 `amount` verbatim for both quote and validation, so a buyer could set their own price.

findings.claim: 0xNexuz/eunomia markets itself as "an accountability layer… trust agents by what they prove" but its trust score is a hardcoded per-agent constant. The identity read and ERC-8183 job lifecycle are real; the scoring is theatre.
findings.detail: app/api/verify/route.ts defines `profiles` as a literal map — "74": baseScore 88.0, "1813": 92.0, "1816": 90.0 — then computes score = baseScore + (capabilityMatched ? 0.4 : -4.8) + (budget<=0.5 ? 0.2 : -2), where capabilityMatched is a substring test OR `task.length > 24`. A longer task string raises the score. What IS real: viem readContract ownerOf + tokenURI against BSC testnet registry (lib/bnb.ts), deterministic hashReceipt over the receipt body, a fail-closed policy gate that blocks a 2.50 USDT budget before any wallet prompt, and an ERC-8183 AgenticCommerce job state machine through EvaluatorRouter + OptimisticPolicy with an optimistic dispute window. 28 files, 4 commits, Next.js + drizzle + Cloudflare Worker. The README is unusually candid about scope, marking the BNB MPP/x402 node as "intentionally disabled until a recipient address and settlement signer are configured; Eunomia does not pretend a challenge is paid."

findings.claim: gilbertsahumada/bnb-agent-marketplace is the best-architected TypeScript entrant — hexagonal layering, 20 test files, and the only one wiring a third-party trust provider (trust8004) behind a repository port.
findings.detail: 59 commits, 142 files. src/business/{entities,use-cases,policies,errors} separated from src/data/{repositories,proofs,cache} and src/presentation/http — with tests/frontend-boundaries.test.ts enforcing that layering. Two agent repositories behind one interface: marketplace-agent-repository.ts and trust8004-marketplace-agent-repository.ts. src/verification/onchain.ts uses viem with an explicit assertChain() that throws on `chainId !== 56`, reads at a pinned blockNumber (readIdentity(agentId, blockNumber)) — the right primitive for reproducible evidence — over an ABI of ownerOf / getAgentWallet / tokenURI. src/trust8004/ has provider.ts, schemas.ts (parsed, not trusted), classify.ts, types.ts with TRUST8004_BASE_URL = "https://trust8004.xyz" and CATALOG_COVERAGE = "partial" — coverage is a declared first-class value, not a hidden assumption. UI carries evidence-rail.tsx, provenance-badge.tsx, public-proof-page.tsx. Notably it hardcodes a single proof route: app/api/marketplace/proofs/jobs/514/route.ts and src/data/proofs/gate1-job-514.ts — one real job, generalized later.

findings.claim: TermiX AACP — the hackathon's own partner — already runs a staked-evaluator protocol on BSC with four evaluation strategies including TEE + Groth16 zkVM proof for capital-handling agents. Its documented testnet backend was returning 503 when I probed it.
findings.detail: TermiX-official/termix-agent-skills (public, 3 commits, 26 files, pushed 2026-05-14) documents the live protocol. docs/register-evaluator.md: evaluator strategy types 0 PROGRAM ("programmatic evaluation via program hash"), 1 RUBRIC, 2 HYBRID, 3 CEX_CAPITAL ("CEX trading — TEE-secured execution + Groth16 zkVM proof"); registration is IMMUTABLE once set; minimum 100 USDC staked via AACPStaking.deposit(); agent must hold an Agent NFT. Skill set covers register-agent, register-provider, register-evaluator, client-create-job, client-set-provider, provider-submit-offer, provider-submit, check-dispute. Base URL https://aacp-backend.termix.live/api/v1 with /config (live contract addresses — docs explicitly say "Do not hardcode it"), /agents/{id} exposing stakingPool + evaluatorCapability, /jobs/{id}/dispute, /disputes. CAUTION: my direct GET to /api/v1/config and /api/v1/stats both returned nginx 503 on 18 Aug 2026 ~21:30 UTC — the documented testnet backend was down. Separately, news reports (MARKETING, unverified by me) say TermiX launched mainnet plus an Agent.family marketplace on BNB Chain.

findings.claim: RNWY ships the most sophisticated sybil-detection surface in the category — reviewer-side provenance analysis, not just agent-side scoring — free and keyless at https://rnwy.com/api/agents.
findings.detail: Direct call today returns per-agent: overall_score plus component scores address_age_score, network_score, continuity_score, activity_score, commerce_score, and score_breakdown. Crucially it also returns REVIEWER-side sybil signals, which nobody else exposes: feedbacker_age_label, feedbacker_avg_age, feedbacker_pct_fresh, reviewer_unique_ratio, feedbacker_bucket_counts, feedbacker_no_history, feedbacker_total_checked, feedbacker_computed_at. Plus identity continuity (is_original_owner, transfer_count, original_owner), capability introspection (mcp_endpoint, a2a_endpoint, mcp_tools, a2a_skills, mcp_version, a2a_version, capabilities_fetched_at), and x402_support, supported_trusts, agent_wallet, ens, did, vouch_count. Search results describe coverage as 150,000+ agents across 10 chains with no API key. Note the same filter trap: ?chain_id=56 returned a chain_id 100 record, so the correct BSC filter parameter is unknown to me — that is a gap.

findings.claim: daluoboda/agentlens and alogotron/assay-bsc are both abandoned or pre-implementation, but assay-bsc contributes the single sharpest strategic insight in the whole cohort: the registry is bimodal, so recency-ranking surfaces only unproven agents.
findings.detail: agentlens: 2 commits, last pushed 2026-08-11 (a week stale). backend/app/chain_data.py holds correct BSC TESTNET addresses — IDENTITY 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e (I confirmed 130 bytes of code onchain), REPUTATION 0x8004B663056A597Dffe9eCcC1965A193B7388713, VALIDATION 0x8004Cb1BF31DAf7788923b405b754f57acEB4272 — and correct ABI fragments (tokenURI, ownerOf, getAgentWallet, agentExists, addFeedback). Its own HACKATHON_GAP_ANALYSIS.md (in Chinese) self-diagnoses the fatal flaw: 性能数据是模拟的，不是真实链上数据 ("performance data is simulated, not real onchain data") and calls the mock TermiX report a 致命问题 ("fatal problem"). assay-bsc: 1 commit, 20 of 23 files are raw probe JSON; README says "marketplace interface not yet implemented". But its census finding is the best framing anyone produced: of the 500 most recently registered BSC agents, 0 had feedback; of the 300 earliest, 297 had feedback and 273 declared x402 support — "Ranking by recency surfaces almost exclusively unproven entries." It also states its own sampling limit honestly (800 of 247,808 = 0.3%).

findings.claim: Broader category: Olas Mech Marketplace, Virtuals ACP and Fetch.ai all solved agent-hires-agent commerce years before ERC-8004, but none of them anchor authority to measured competence — assessed from secondary sources only.
findings.detail: MARKETING/secondary, not primary docs — I did not fetch the specs, so treat as low confidence. Olas Mech Marketplace: contracts registering mechs and relaying request/delivery, per-request payment in native token or OLAS, a Nevermined subscription model where the quoted value is max price per request, a balance-tracker contract from which mechs periodically withdraw with a DAO fee burned; reference implementation at github.com/valory-xyz/autonolas-marketplace. Olas publicly stated in 2026 that marketplace agents surpassed 10M+ (interactions). Virtuals ACP: a four-phase model — Request, Negotiation, Transaction, Evaluation — with Client/Provider/Evaluator roles, escrow held until an Evaluator verifies work against a cryptographically signed Proof of Agreement; ACP v2 made the evaluation phase OPTIONAL, which is the tell that evaluation was friction rather than the product. Python SDK virtuals-acp released 2026-03-03. Fetch.ai/Agentverse: no primary source fetched — full gap. Common shape: all three treat evaluation as a per-job settlement gate, none carry a durable, portable competence record across jobs.

gaps: Fetch.ai / Agentverse: not investigated at all. No primary doc fetched, no API probed. Complete blind spot in the survey.

"Agent Veil" and "agentscan": searched, no primary source found. Agent Veil returned zero relevant results — it may not exist under that name, may be private, or may be too new to index. agentscan likewise unresolved (8004scan.io is a different product). Do not assume they are absent; assume unmeasured.

Olas Mech Marketplace and Virtuals ACP were assessed from search-result summaries and one Delphi/whitepaper link list — I fetched NEITHER primary doc and probed NEITHER contract. No contract addresses, no function signatures, no fee parameters verified. Everything in that finding is secondary and tagged low confidence.

TermiX AACP contract addresses are unknown. The docs deliberately instruct fetching them from GET /api/v1/config at runtime, and that endpoint returned nginx 503 when I called it. AACPStaking, the job/escrow contract, and the evaluator registry addresses are all unretrieved. The claimed TermiX MAINNET launch and Agent.family marketplace are news-report claims I did not verify onchain.

RNWY's correct BSC chain filter parameter is unknown — ?chain_id=56 returned a Gnosis (chain 100) record. Total RNWY coverage of chain 56 is therefore unmeasured, and the "150,000+ agents across 10 chains" figure is from a search snippet, not a counted API response.

trust8004.xyz's scoring methodology is a black box. I observed the output shape (dimensions + confidence floats) but have no documentation for how `confidence` is derived, what `availability` actually probes, what the tier thresholds are, or what `chaosChain` and `activeReputationSystems` connect to. No OpenAPI spec found at that host.

8004scan's POST /agents/{chain_id}/{token_id}/health-check requires authentication (returned {"detail":"Authentication required"}), so I could not observe what a liveness probe actually measures — protocol, timeout, retry policy, or how health_status maps to the score. Same for POST /agents/verify-endpoint/{chain_id}/{token_id}.

The ERC-8004 spec text itself (eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004) was never fetched. All registry semantics here are inferred from third-party ABIs in competitor repos (agentlens chain_data.py, gilbertsahumada onchain.ts). ValidationRegistry's actual interface — the function signatures AiKi would have to implement — is unread.

winsznx/mandate's AuthorityIR schema, ScopeHashLib hashing scheme, and MandateReceiptRegistry.sol implementation body were not read — only the interface file IMandateReceiptRegistry.sol and one evidence bundle. The subset-relation check that makes the authority-ceiling claim meaningful is unexamined. Given this repo was created 18 Aug 2026 and is moving fast, re-check it.

AgentEra's two claimed Altana txs (grant 0x59ff5f93…, revoke 0x7f0caa06…) and Ai-Rook's claimed BSC anchoring txs were NOT verified onchain. I verified only kaizenbnb's work tx and mandate's deploy tx.

The arXiv sybil/manipulation figures are peer research measured through 13 May 2026. BSC has grown from 90,145 to 257,906 agents since — a 2.9× increase. The 96.3% sybil rate and $0.0042 attack cost may have moved in either direction and were not re-measured.

No competitor's UI was actually loaded. All live-deployment claims (ai-rook.com/bnb-marketplace, eunomia-ai.vercel.app, agentera-kappa.vercel.app, bnb-agent-marketplace.vercel.app) are README assertions, unverified.
aiki_implications: HONEST ANSWER TO YOUR FRAMING QUESTION: yes, someone is already doing it — three someones, in pieces. trust8004 ships confidence-weighted scoring, 8004scan ships liveness + explainable multi-dimension scoring, winsznx/mandate ships trial-derived benchmarks AND mandate enforcement tiers on-chain. All four of your named differentiators exist in production or in a deployed hackathon repo as of today. The evidence layer as stated is not a differentiator. What is NOT solved is composition: nobody binds a measured competence record to an enforceable spend authority that a third party can independently re-derive. mandate is the closest and it is 8 hours old.

REBUILDING SCORING IS THE #1 WASTE RISK. Do not write a trust-score algorithm. trust8004's /api/v2/agents/{id}/score returns per-dimension {score, weight, weighted, confidence} for chainId 56, keyless, with a 5-minute TTL, and 8004scan's scores/v5 returns a weighted 5-dimension breakdown with explanation strings. Consume both, disagree with them explicitly, and ship the DELTA as your product: a score-of-scores that shows where the two incumbents diverge and why. That is a position neither can occupy.

THE VALIDATION REGISTRY IS THE ACTUAL MOAT. total_validations: 0, total_validators: 0, against 743,130 agents and 3.55M feedbacks. Every incumbent is competing on reputation (subjective, saturated, 96.3% sybil on BSC, $0.0042 to manipulate). Nobody is on validation (objective, empty, zero incumbents). If AiKi's evidence layer writes to the ValidationRegistry rather than reading the ReputationRegistry, you are the first mover on the half of ERC-8004 the entire ecosystem skipped. Fetch the EIP text first — I did not, and its interface is your build spec.

STEAL mandate's `freshUntil` AND `testedAuthorityHash` SHAPE, DO NOT REINVENT IT. A receipt that expires converts liveness from a poll into a contract invariant, and an authority CEILING that a failed trial can never back (error ReceiptDidNotPass, enforced on-chain) is exactly the mandate-tier semantics you wanted. Also copy its `disclosureURI` reasoning: a hash alone lets a verifier CHECK a document they were handed but never OBTAIN one, so an independent verifier working from chain alone cannot evaluate the subset relation. Any AiKi mandate record needs both the commitment and the retrieval path.

BUILD ON ANVIL FORK-REPLAY, NOT ON SELF-REPORTED HEALTH ENDPOINTS. mandate's evidence-bundle.json is the template: pin forkBlock + forkBlockHash, declare rpcSourceClass, enumerate EVERY state modification (anvil_setBalance, anvil_impersonateAccount) with the explicit disclaimer that no signature was produced, and run named boolean checks against an independent reference model. Its `observation-is-current` check — did the agent reason about the block the trial presented — is the single best liveness primitive I saw anywhere, because it is unfakeable by a cached response. Ai-Rook's competing approach (curl your own localhost:3051 and call it verified) is exactly what to avoid.

INGESTION HARDENING IS NON-NEGOTIABLE AND CHEAP. 8004scan's chain filter is `chain_id`; `chain=56` and `chain_ids=56` are SILENTLY IGNORED and return Ethereum agents. RNWY's ?chain_id=56 returned a Gnosis record. 0xConsole shipped this bug. Assert the returned chain_id on every row, reject the batch on mismatch, and never trust a query parameter you have not seen echoed in the payload. Same discipline for addresses: AgentEra's fabricated evidence was detectable purely because a pool address was 39 hex chars — length-validate every address at ingest and you catch synthetic data for free.

DO NOT SCORE THE WHOLE REGISTRY — IT IS 96% NOISE AND SCORING IT IS THE TRAP EVERY ENTRANT FELL INTO. Only ~4% of BSC agents have a live service endpoint; 77.9% of rated agents have zero valid feedback after sybil removal; the registration front is bulk-registered bots. kaizenbnb reached the right conclusion and wrote it down: they refused to wire the home page to the live registry because it would show noise, not a comparison. AiKi should define an explicit admission gate (endpoint answers + a passed trial + a funded wallet with history) and publish the gate. Coverage is a feature to declare, not hide — gilbertsahumada made CATALOG_COVERAGE = "partial" a typed constant.

RECENCY RANKING IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL HERE — assay-bsc's census is the finding to internalize: of the 500 newest BSC agents, 0 had feedback; of the 300 oldest, 297 had feedback and 273 declared x402. Sorting by registration date surfaces exclusively unproven entries. Your default sort must be evidence-derived from day one, and your cold-start story for a genuinely new good agent has to be a TRIAL, not a waiting period — which is precisely why the benchmark layer earns its cost.

PAYMENT RAILS ARE SOLVED — CLONE, DO NOT DESIGN. Ai-Rook's b402.js is a complete, working reference for Binance's authenticated facilitator: RSA-SHA256 signing over body+timestamp, X-Tesla-{ClientId,SignAccessToken,Timestamp,Signature} headers, /papi/v2/b402/verify then /papi/v2/b402/settle, envelope.code '000000', fail-closed on settlement. Altana session keys (call allowlist + spend cap + expiry + on-chain Keystore + user revoke) are demonstrated in two independent repos. Budget days for this, not weeks — and take kaizenbnb's warning: fix the price server-side, because a client-supplied x402 `amount` used verbatim for both quote and validation lets a buyer set their own price.

YOUR REAL COMPETITOR IS TERMIX, NOT THE HACKATHON COHORT. AACP already has staked evaluators (100 USDC minimum), immutable strategy-type registration, PROGRAM/RUBRIC/HYBRID/CEX_CAPITAL tiers with TEE + Groth16 zkVM for capital-handling agents, a full job lifecycle, and a dispute system — and TermiX is simultaneously the bounty sponsor scoring the entrants. Position AiKi as the evidence SUPPLIER to AACP evaluators rather than a competing marketplace; a PROGRAM-strategy evaluator needs exactly the reproducible trial artifact you intend to produce. Verify their mainnet contracts first — their documented testnet backend was 503 today.

SHIP HONESTY AS A FEATURE — IT IS SCARCE AND IT IS SCORED. The strongest entrants (kaizenbnb, alogotron, gilbertsahumada) win on candor: labeled ESTIMATE vs measured, stated sampling limits (0.3% of the registry), a refusal to split an unmeasured 28.5s into guesses, disclosed shared wallets. The weakest (AgentEra, eunomia's hardcoded baseScore, agentlens' own admission that its data is 模拟的) fabricate. Since AiKi's entire pitch is an evidence layer, a single unlabeled synthetic number anywhere in the product is disqualifying in a way it would not be for a pure marketplace. Adopt alogotron's rule verbatim: every rendered metric traces to an on-chain transaction, an API response field, or a logged run, with provenance displayed beside the value.

interfaces.body:
# Register Evaluator
Register agent `$agent_id` as an Evaluator for strategy type `$strategy_type` on-chain.

> **Warning: This registration is IMMUTABLE.** Once set, the strategy type cannot be changed.

**Strategy types:**
| Value | Name          | Description |
|-------|---------------|-------------|
| `0`   | `PROGRAM`     | Programmatic evaluation via program hash |
| `1`   | `RUBRIC`      | Rubric-based scoring |
| `2`   | `HYBRID`      | Combined program + rubric |
| `3`   | `CEX_CAPITAL` | CEX trading — TEE-secured execution + Groth16 zkVM proof |

**Prerequisites:**
- Agent must hold a valid Agent NFT
- Minimum **100 USDC staked** (`AACPStaking.deposit()`)

### 1. Fetch live contract addresses
curl -s "https://aacp-backend.termix.live/api/v1/config" | jq '.data.contracts'
Note `AACPStaking` address. **Success criteria:** Address retrieved from live config.
Do not hardcode it.

### 2. Check current agent state
curl -s "https://aacp-backend.termix.live/api/v1/agents/$agent_id" \
  | jq '{stakingPool: .data.stakingPool, evaluatorCapability: .data.evaluatorCapability}'
- If `stakingPool.available` < `"100000000"` → run `/register-provider` first.

# Dispute routes (docs/check-dispute.md)
#   GET /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/dispute
#   GET /api/v1/disputes/{disputeId}
#   GET /api/v1/disputes?jobId={jobId}
# fields: disputeId, jobId, …
